The role stays engaged as priorities and conditions evolve, using evidence and insights to help teams adapt while maintaining alignment to intended outcomes. Support transparent investment and prioritization decisions through clear analysis, evidence, and recommendations. Help teams balance near-term delivery needs with longer-term strategic outcomes and organizational sustainability. Connect information across functions to support coordinated action without creating unnecessary layers of approval or reporting. Distinguish activity and deliverables from meaningful progress toward desired outcomes. Use evidence, stakeholder insight, and organizational learning to inform ongoing prioritization and roadmap decisions. Facilitate periodic assessment of whether priorities and investments remain relevant and positioned to create the intended value. Support informed decisions about where to continue, change, accelerate, pause, or stop based on evidence and changing conditions. Translate complex or fragmented information into clear scenarios, recommendations, and decision materials. Bring a broader enterprise perspective to decisions while respecting the expertise and accountability of functional and business leaders. Build trusted relationships across the Society that enable candid dialogue, collaboration, and effective decision-making. Support executive portfolio and business reviews with concise, forward-looking insights and recommendations. Identify where site-specific constraints or customer requirements demand a departure from the commissioning standard, and route deviations through the established Technical Strategy & Architecture approval process. Own the technical integrity of commissioning milestones and readiness assessments, even where schedule development is delegated — commissioning dates in the plan must reflect what the systems and test program can actually support. Maintain a forward view of commissioning readiness across assigned campuses, flagging cross-project resource or sequencing conflicts to regional leadership before they become delivery risks. Review and validate commissioning plans, test scripts, and procedures across electrical, mechanical, and controls systems, ensuring alignment with GD&E design standards, project design documents, and customer requirements. Oversee system-level testing through Integrated Systems Testing (IST), including failure mode validation, ensuring every system performs to specification. Support vendor and equipment validation — witnessing Factory Acceptance Tests (FAT) at vendor facilities and confirming that what was validated in the factory is what performs in the field. Provide onsite commissioning leadership during critical phases — startup, functional testing, IST, and energization — with presence concentrated at whichever assigned campus is in an active commissioning window. Monitor commissioning activities for compliance with safety, quality, and environmental standards, and stop or escalate testing when conditions or results warrant it. Ensure commissioning documentation is complete, accurate, and maintained to GD&E standards within company systems (e.g., CxAlloy, Compass, or equivalent) throughout the project lifecycle. Provide clear, timely reporting on commissioning status, risks, and readiness to the site TPM/DM team and regional leadership, aligned to GD&E's stage-gate governance and reporting cadence. Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a closely related engineering discipline — required. Certifications: PMP strongly preferred; BCxA CCP or ACG CxA valued; CDCP or CDCDP preferred; NETA Level II or higher desired. Experience 8+ years of progressive experience in data center or mission-critical engineering, construction, or commissioning, with proven experience leading commissioning on large-scale, mission-critical data center projects. Demonstrated experience taking hyperscale / Tier III+ facilities through the full commissioning lifecycle — from Cx planning in design through FAT, startup, functional testing, IST, energization, and handover. Experience coordinating with EPC / execution partner field teams and third-party commissioning planners and agents — driving readiness and quality through influence within an integrated site team. Familiarity with commissioning platforms such as CxAlloy, Compass, or equivalent. Deep understanding of mission-critical data center systems: electrical distribution (MV/LV, switchgear, UPS, generators), mechanical systems (cooling plants, CRAH/CRAC, fluid systems), and controls (BMS/EPMS integration). Deep familiarity with commissioning methodology: pre-functional and functional testing, Integrated Systems Testing (IST), failure mode validation, readiness criteria, and performance validation. Working knowledge of construction-driven scheduling tools (Primavera P6, MS Project) with the ability to interrogate schedule logic and challenge commissioning durations and dependencies. Clear, concise communication, with the credibility to deliver a "not ready" call and the discipline to back it with data and a recovery path. Comfort operating across multiple concurrent campuses in a fast-paced, high-growth environment where the portfolio is expanding and processes are maturing. Travel Significant travel required (50–75%) across assigned campuses in EMEA, including extended onsite presence during startup, functional testing, and IST phases, plus travel to vendor facilities for FAT — concentrated around commissioning windows and occasionally at short notice.
